title: Classes and circles
hook: learning in person or online with others
tomorrow: what turns a dinner table into something holy?

segments.voice: Yesterday, five Hebrew words, and a page that starts to light up. More Hebrew. Today, the room you learn them in, and who's sitting there with you.

A club fair: folding tables, sign-up sheets, free cookies for anyone who'll stop. At a college open house, Noa collects flyers. A Hillel class on Tuesdays. And from the Muslim students, a flyer for a weekly halaqa, a study circle. Pirkei Avot says that when two people sit together and words of Torah pass between them, the Shekhinah rests between them. The Presence of God. In a class. Between two chairs.
screen: `A TABLE OF FLYERS.` → `A CLASS, AND A CIRCLE.` → `THE PRESENCE, BETWEEN TWO CHAIRS.`

segments.voice: Another teaching in the same chapter counts down: when ten sit and study, the Presence is among them. And five. And three. And two. And even one. So nobody needs a class for the Presence. But the tradition keeps picturing it in a room with others, where words pass between people. Now a neighbor who says something close, in her own tradition's words. In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is reported to have said that when people gather in a house of God, reciting the Book of God and studying it together, tranquility comes down on them, mercy covers them, angels surround them, and God mentions them among those with Him. Shared ground: in both, studying a sacred text together is more than a study session. Something holy settles on the group. And one honest difference. That hadith pictures the gathering in a mosque, with the Qur'an at its center. Pirkei Avot pictures two people anywhere, with Torah between them, and even one person alone. Each tradition, its own book, its own room. Something to tell a friend tonight: Pirkei Avot says God's presence can rest between two people reading together.
screen: `TEN, FIVE, THREE, TWO, ONE.` · `A ROOM WITH OTHERS.` · `ISLAM: TRANQUILITY COMES DOWN.` · `SHARED GROUND, HONEST DIFFERENCE.` · then, large: `LEARN TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Look up one class or study circle near you or online: at a synagogue, a library, a community center, a college. Save the details, or send one message asking when it meets. That's the whole act for now; going can come later.
screen: `ONE CLASS OR CIRCLE.` · `SAVE IT, OR ASK WHEN.` · `GOING CAN COME LATER.`

segments.voice: Classes and circles: learning with others, in person or online, where words pass between people and, the tradition says, the Presence rests among them.
Keep this: learn together. Two chairs are enough for the Presence. Until the next one.

howItsDone: Jewish adults learn together in synagogue classes, study circles, campus groups and online courses; Pirkei Avot teaches that the Shekhinah rests among those who study Torah together.

fork.setup: your new roommate is Muslim and goes to a weekly halaqa. she asks if Jews have anything like it. what's an honest answer?
options: yes: we study together too; Avot says the Presence rests between two who learn.
not really: Jewish study is always done alone, with a book.
yes, it's exactly the same thing, just with a different book.
fork.reveal: both traditions picture something holy settling on people who study together; each has its own book, room and words for it. shared, not the same.

chat.says: found a hillel tuesday class AND a video class. video is way easier. does that even count?
options: It counts. Two with Torah between them is enough; pick the one you'll keep.
No. Only an in-person class counts; a screen can't hold the Presence.
Skip both. Studying alone is enough; groups are for beginners.
chat.meaning: Pirkei Avot says the Presence rests between even two who study Torah together. What matters is learning with others, steadily.

Shekhinah.meaning: the Presence of God, dwelling among people

Pirkei Avot.meaning: a book of the Mishnah: sayings of the sages

halaqa.meaning: Arabic: a circle; a Muslim study circle

Hillel.meaning: here, a Jewish student organization on college campuses

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a collection of hadith, sayings of the Prophet Muhammad

hadith.meaning: a report of the words or deeds of the Prophet Muhammad

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 3:2 (Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon: two who sit and words of Torah are between them, the Shekhinah rests among them)
Mishnah Avot 3:6 (Rabbi Chalafta ben Dosa: ten who sit and study, the Shekhinah is among them; and five, three, two, even one)

Sahih Muslim 2699 (no people gather in a house of God reciting and studying the Book of God among themselves but tranquility descends on them, mercy covers them, angels surround them, and God mentions them among those with Him)
